answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut and 14-day renewal window create severe time and financial pressure. Switching vendors (memory_c2 showed cost gains but took onboarding time we lack) or adding a second source (memory_c3) would introduce delivery risk at 94% line utilization. Deferring (memory_c5) risks losing negotiating leverage at renewal. The incumbent relationship is stable (memory_c1). Memory_c4 demonstrated that renegotiation at renewal recovered margin through benchmarking; memory_c6 showed multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing. A focused renegotiation targeting both unit cost reduction (via benchmarking against low-cost vendor rates from memory_c2) and extended term commitment (to access volume pricing from memory_c6) offers the best path to the 18% target while preserving delivery continuity. We verify memory_c4 to confirm the benchmarking approach's effectiveness. The 14-day deadline is tight but renegotiation is faster than vendor switch or onboarding. Flagging downstream risk: if renegotiation fails, we have no fallback with 10 days remaining. This preserves uncertainty by committing to negotiation rather than irreversible vendor change.
